title: Death's Messengers
summary: In ancient times, a robust young giant was traveling along the highway when he encountered Death sitting exhausted by the roadside, having been beaten in a duel with a mighty champ...
full_text:
In ancient times, a robust young giant was traveling along the highway when he encountered Death sitting exhausted by the roadside, having been beaten in a duel with a mighty champion. The compassionate young man revived Death with fresh spring water and helped him to his feet.

In gratitude, Death promised: "I cannot spare you when your appointed hour strikes, for my duty is universal. But this I swear: I will never come upon you unawares. I shall send my messengers ahead to announce my coming, so you may be ready."

Years passed into decades. The young man grew into a prosperous citizen, enjoying health, wine, and laughter. But gradually, his hair turned silver, his eyesight dimmed, his joints began to ache with winter frost, and a dull ringing settled in his ears. Yet he remained carefree, thinking, "Death has not arrived; he has not sent his heralds!"

At last, a cold tap touched his shoulder, and Death stood before him. "It is time," Death declared.

"False friend!" cried the man. "Did you not swear to send messengers before taking me?"

"Foolish man," answered Death softly. "Have I not sent them every single year? Did not gray hair, failing vision, aching bones, and heavy breath knock upon your door? Every pain, every wrinkle, every weary step was my messenger whispering: prepare your house, for the evening draws near." The man bowed his head in humble understanding, and accompanied his guide into peace.
moral: The aches and changes of aging are gentle warnings to prepare the soul with wisdom and kindness.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "Death's Messengers"?
options: Presence of mind and quiet wisdom triumph over brute strength.
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof

By running away from every problem
